bib.title: Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2024 (38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: References skimmed only. Figure 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 chart values are garbled in the text layer and not recorded as results.

question: Can storing distilled high-level thought-templates from solved problems and retrieving them for new problems improve LLM reasoning accuracy, efficiency and robustness over single-query and multi-query prompting?
hypothesis: High-level thought-templates shared across tasks let an LLM skip building a reasoning structure from scratch, improving accuracy and efficiency.
contributions: A thought-augmented reasoning framework, Buffer of Thoughts (BoT), for accuracy, efficiency and robustness.
A meta-buffer that stores high-level thoughts distilled from different problems and instantiates them per task.
A buffer-manager that distils thought-templates from solutions and grows the meta-buffer as more tasks are solved.
Experiments on 10 reasoning-intensive tasks with SOTA gains over prior prompting methods at about 12% of multi-query cost.

method.summary: A prompting pipeline with no training. A problem-distiller LLM call extracts variables and constraints; the distilled text is embedded and matched by cosine-style similarity to descriptions of stored thought-templates in a meta-buffer; the retrieved template is instantiated by an LLM (often as code or a stepwise procedure); a buffer-manager distils a new template from the solution and adds it if it is not too similar to existing ones.
method.task: Prompt-based reasoning over Game of 24, BBH tasks, Checkmate-in-One, Penguins, Date Understanding, P3, MGSM and sonnet writing

other.note: Base model for main experiment and ablations
Used in analysis on NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB

inference.samples: Main table: not stated. Robustness: 1000 random examples from various benchmarks, evaluation repeated 10 times, average accuracy reported as success rate.
inference.prompting: Problem-distiller meta prompt (A.2), instantiation prompt (A.3), template-distillation prompt (Sec 3.3) with optional in-task or cross-task exemplars. Six template categories: Text Comprehension, Creative Language Generation, Common Sense Reasoning, Mathematical Reasoning, Code Programming, Application Scheduling.
inference.retrieval: Embedding similarity between distilled problem and template descriptions; argmax with threshold delta (0.5 to 0.7 recommended); below threshold the task is new and one of three general coarse-grained templates is assigned. Embedding model: 'a normal text embedding model', not named. Meta-buffer starts empty in the analyses.

parameters.update_rule: Add new template only if Max(Sim(f(DT_new), {f(DT_i)})) < delta

prompts.text:
User: [Problem Description] + [Solution Steps or Code]
To extract and summarize the high-level paradigms and general approaches for solving such problems, please follow these steps in your response:
1. Core task summarization ... 2. Solution Steps Description ... 3. General Answer Template ...

As a highly professional and intelligent expert in information distillation, you excel at extracting essential information to solve problems from user input queries. ... 1. Key information ... 2. Restrictions ... 3. Distilled task
You are a Meta Reasoner who are extremely knowledgeable in all kinds of fields ... If the thought-template is provided, directly follow the thought-template to instantiate for the given problem.

results.claim: BoT with GPT-4 scores 82.4% on Game of 24, above ToT, GoT, PAL, Meta Prompting and CoT.
results.setup: GPT-4 base, Table 1, Game of 24 from ToT; baselines: GPT-4 3.0, CoT 11.0, Expert 3.0, PAL 64.0, ToT 74.0, GoT 73.2, Meta Prompting 67.0
results.quote: compared to ToT, which has a good performance on this task, we also achieve an 8.4% accuracy improvement
results.table: Table 1, row Game of 24, column BoT (Ours)
results.note: Abstract says 11% over previous SOTA on Game of 24; Sec 4.1 says 23% over Meta Prompting (82.4 vs 67.0 = 15.4 points). Both gaps are inconsistent with Table 1 for Meta Prompting.

results.claim: BoT requires about 12% of the cost of multi-query methods on average.
results.setup: Inference-time comparison in Fig 3 covers Game of 24, MGSM and Checkmate-in-One only, GPT-4; cost measured as time, not tokens or dollars; compared with ToT and meta-prompting.
results.quote: Notably, our BoT requires only 12% of the cost of multi-query methods (e.g., tree of thoughts and meta-prompting) on average.
results.note: How 12% is averaged is not stated.

results.claim: BoT reaches 86.4% on Checkmate-in-One versus 57.2% for Meta Prompting.
results.setup: GPT-4 base, Table 1; ToT 49.2, GoT 51.4, GPT-4 36.4
results.quote: 20% on Geometric Shapes and 51% on Checkmate-in-One
results.note: Gap is 29.2 points against Meta Prompting; 51% is the abstract's number and does not match Table 1 for that baseline (86.4-36.4=50.0 vs plain GPT-4).

results.claim: BoT reaches 93.6% on Geometric Shapes versus 78.2% for Meta Prompting.
results.table: Table 1, row Geometric Shapes, column BoT (Ours)
results.note: Gap is 15.4 points; the text says 20%.

results.claim: BoT is best on all ten tasks in Table 1; margin is smallest on Sonnet Writing (80.0 vs 79.6) and Word Sorting (100.0 vs 99.6).
results.setup: GPT-4 base, Sonnet Writing, Table 1; single run, no variance reported
results.table: Table 1, row Sonnet Writing, column BoT (Ours)
results.note: Margins of 0.4 points on a creative task are within plausible noise; paper reports none.

results.claim: Robustness: BoT beats the second-best method by 10% in average success rate.
results.setup: 1000 random examples from various benchmarks, repeated 10 times, averaged; Game of 24, MGSM, Checkmate-in-One (Fig 4).
results.quote: surpassing the second-best by 10% in average success rate

results.claim: With the buffer-manager, BoT+GPT4 accuracy rises across four rounds while it stays flat without it.
results.setup: Read from Fig 9: round 4, 50 randomly sampled questions per benchmark per round, GPT-4; without buffer-manager the final round is 54.1
results.quote: the accuracy of BoT steadily improves with each round
results.note: Values read from garbled chart text; series assignment is inferred.

results.claim: BoT+Llama3-8B has the potential to surpass Llama3-70B alone.
results.setup: Game of 24, word list sorting, Checkmate-in-One; Llama3-8B and 70B on A100; Fig 6 values garbled
results.quote: Notably, BoT+Llama3-8B has the potential to surpass single Llama3-70B model.
results.note: Hedged wording ('potential'); per-task numbers cannot be read reliably.

results.claim: Disabling the problem-distiller or the meta-buffer lowers accuracy, most on Game of 24 and Checkmate-in-One.
results.setup: Llama3-70B and GPT-4 base, four benchmarks (Game of 24, word list sorting, Checkmate-in-One, MGSM), Figs 7 and 8
results.quote: More complex problems, such as Game of 24 and Checkmate-in-One, show a more significant accuracy reduction

limits: Authors concede enhancements are limited for problems needing human-like creativity, which do not rely on a specific thought-template.
Authors concede a weaker model initialising the meta-buffer may derive suboptimal templates.
Table 1 is a single GPT-4 run with no variance, decoding settings, sample counts or test-set sizes given.
Cost claim rests on time over three tasks (Fig 3), not tokens or dollars; the 12% averaging is unspecified.
Embedding model, threshold delta actually used, and meta-buffer initial contents are not stated.
Template sharing across tasks was shown on benchmarks the buffer was built from; no held-out-task transfer test is reported beyond in-task and cross-task exemplars.
Headline gains in the abstract (11%, 20%, 51%) do not match Table 1 consistently.

terms.definition: a lightweight library that contains a series of high-level thoughts (thought-template) for addressing various types of problems
a kind of high-level guideline stored in the meta-buffer, obtained from problem-solving processes by the buffer-manager
summarizes the high-level guidelines and thoughts gained from each problem-solving process and stores them as thought-templates
extracts critical task-specific information along with relevant constraints before reasoning
average accuracy over 10 repeats of evaluation on a 1000-example random subset, used to assess reasoning robustness
